items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: A couple of years, because after her was when I joined Benny Carter.

ctx.x: You were with her for a couple of years, right?
A couple of years, because after her was when I joined Benny Carter. About '33, '34, something like that.
I'm forgetting, were you on the record that Benny made of Spike Hughes' arrangements, the British arranger?

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I had people in it like Cozy Cole, Big Sid Catlett, Dickie Wells, Chu Chew Berry.

ctx.x: Yes. What kind of ... or did you have dates right off or was it a band that you formed with the idea of doing whatever you could -- it wasn't formed to sign a contract or to do something?
No, it was hoping to be able to do something after getting the band together, and it was really, essentially, a rehearsal band, you know?

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Before, huh? It may have been, yeah. Cozy Cole, and at one point Sid Catlett.

ctx.x: Was there a period that you formed this band without any regard to work, I mean, just as something to play music?

Yes. I’m wondering if that might have been during that time or whether it might have been after that time. I know that I did have a rehearsal band, and Chu Berry and . . . I think that was around 1933, though. Did I?
Well, I think by 1933 the band was already working and recording, and I think this rehearsal period may have been that earlier stage in ’32.
